title: Keep a carrier outage from failing a label booking

blocks.text: The warehouse books a shipping label for every parcel through the carrier's API. Addresses come from customers' typing, so the carrier sometimes rejects one, and `ship(...)` then hands the parcel to `bookNormalized(...)`, which tries once more with the address cleaned up.

During last week's carrier incident, the packing stations showed a stack trace instead of the usual "retry later" for every parcel that had needed a second attempt. And a parcel whose address was wrong in both forms must go to the address-review queue, where a person fixes it; it must not come back every ten minutes.
`ship(...)` already books, and already answers a carrier failure on the first attempt. Finish the `TODO` in `src/main/java/practice/LabelBooking.java`:

items: `bookNormalized(...)`: book the parcel with `normalize(address)` and return what `ship(...)` returns: `"booked: "` and the tracking number, `"review: "` and the carrier's reason when the address is rejected again, or `"retry later: "` and the message when the carrier fails.

blocks.text: `ship(...)` never throws a carrier failure at its caller. About six lines in total.
The tests use a scripted carrier, with addresses and failures of their own.

cases.says: a rejected address is booked again in its normalized form, and the booking's tracking number is returned
when the normalized address is rejected too, the parcel goes to review with the carrier's second reason
when the carrier fails during the second attempt, ship() returns retry later instead of throwing

origin.section: An Exception Thrown in a Catch Block Leaves the Whole try Statement

concepts: An exception thrown inside a catch block leaves the whole try statement; the catch clauses below it never see it.
